title: Gluing locally finitely presented immersion representatives
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For each morphism $g:T\to S$ let $P(g)$ be a proposition. Suppose $P(g)$ implies $P(g\circ h)$ for every $h:T'\to T$, and suppose $P(g)$ holds whenever every point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ with $P(g\circ\iota_V)$. Assume that for each $s\in S$ there exist an open neighbourhood $U$, a scheme $W_U$, and an immersion locally of finite presentation $j_U:W_U\to U$ representing the predicate: for all $g:T\to U$, $g$ factors through $j_U$ if and only if $P(\iota_U\circ g)$. Then there exist a scheme $W$ and an immersion locally of finite presentation $j:W\to S$ with, for all $g:T\to S$, $g$ factors through $j$ if and only if $P(g)$.

proof.text: Forget the local finite-presentation witnesses and apply the existing local immersion locus theorem to P, hbase, hsource and the remaining local witnesses. Obtain an immersion q:Z to S with its global representing equivalence. This reuses all gluing and factorization from the existing theorem rather than duplicating its private helper.

Choose the original locally finitely presented representatives j_i:W_i to U_i. For each i let A be the pullback of q along U_i inclusion. The global representing equivalence gives P on A from its first projection, and the local equivalence gives a:A to W_i over U_i. Applying the local equivalence to the identity on W_i gives P(j_i followed by inclusion); the global equivalence yields b:W_i to Z. Lift b and j_i to c:W_i to A. Cancel the monomorphisms j_i and the second pullback projection to prove c followed by a and a followed by c are identities. These are explicit Lean calculations using pullback lift and cancel_mono, and identify the two representatives without any gluing helper.

The second pullback projection equals a followed by j_i. Since a is an isomorphism, composition stability gives local finite presentation of this projection. Form the point-indexed open cover U_i and apply Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_openCover for LocallyOfFinitePresentation. Return q with its original immersion and representing criterion. The point-indexed cover is vacuous for empty S, handled by the same locality theorem.

lean.statement: theorem exists_localFinitelyPresentedImmersionLocus (S : Scheme.{u}) (P : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}}, (T ⟶ S) → Prop) (hbase : ∀ {T T' : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) (h : T' ⟶ T), P g → P (h ≫ g)) (hsource : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S), (∀ t : T, ∃ V : T.Opens, t ∈ V ∧ P (V.ι ≫ g)) → P g) (hlocal : ∀ s : S, ∃ U : S.Opens, s ∈ U ∧ ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ U.toScheme), IsImmersion j ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j ∧ ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ U.toScheme), (∃ h : T ⟶ W, h ≫ j = g) ↔ P (g ≫ U.ι)) : ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ S), IsImmersion j ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j ∧ ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S), (∃ h : T ⟶ W, h ≫ j = g) ↔ P g
